lecture_summary: The lecture develops Newton’s inverse-square law, gravitational acceleration versus altitude, gravitational potential energy, circular-orbit dynamics, Kepler’s laws, and geostationary satellites. Its core problem-solving moves are converting altitude to center-based radius, treating gravity as the inward net force, using v = 2πr/T, solving symbolically, and using ratios to cancel shared constants.

videos.title: Gravity and the Universal Law of Gravitation - Physics
videos.reason: Establishes Newton’s universal gravitation law and connects gravitational force with weight and gravitational acceleration.

videos.title: Gravitational Field Strength
videos.reason: Best match for calculating g at Earth’s surface and at altitude, including the lecture’s crucial use of center-based distance r = R_E + h.

videos.title: Speed of a Satellite in Circular Orbit, Orbital Velocity, Period, Centripetal Force, Physics Problem
videos.reason: Directly applies gravity as the inward net force to derive circular-orbit speed and calculate orbital period—the lecture’s main orbit-solving strategy.

videos.title: Kepler's Third Law of Planetary Motion Explained, Physics Problems, Period & Orbital Radius
videos.reason: Covers T² ∝ r³ and period–radius calculations, matching the derivation and ratio method used in the eight-year-planet example.

coverage_gaps: No listed video strongly matches the derivation and interpretation of U = -GMm/r or the circular-orbit energy results K = GMm/(2r) and E = -GMm/(2r).
Kepler’s first and second laws, including the speed and energy changes along an elliptical orbit, lack a strong match.
No listed video directly covers Newton’s cannon or the conceptual picture of orbit as continuous free fall.

The satellite and Kepler videos provide the mathematical ingredients for geostationary motion, but no listed video explicitly covers all geostationary conditions and the altitude-versus-radius calculation.
The quantitative comparison of electric and gravitational forces between two electrons lacks a strong match.
